subtopics.title: World Environment Day and UNEP
subtopics.summary: World Environment Day is celebrated every year on June 5 and was established in 1972 to coincide with the opening of the Stockholm Conference on Human Environment. It is organised by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), which is based in Nairobi, Kenya. The 2026 edition carried the theme 'Inspired by Nature. For Climate. For Our Future.' and named Azerbaijan as Global Host.
facts: World Environment Day is celebrated on June 5 every year.
Established in 1972 to coincide with the opening of the Stockholm Conference on Human Environment.
Celebrated in 1973 with the theme 'Only One Earth'.
Organised by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP).
UNEP was founded in 1972 and is based in Nairobi, Kenya.
Purpose: raise awareness and drive global action on pressing environmental issues.
WED 2026 theme: 'Inspired by Nature. For Climate. For Our Future.'
Azerbaijan was named Global Host for World Environment Day 2026.

subtopics.title: Global Climate Finance and the Tropical Forest Facility
subtopics.summary: The New Collective Quantified Goal (NCQG) on climate finance was formally established at COP29 in Baku. It sets a target to scale up climate funding for developing nations to at least $1.3 trillion per year by 2035, with developed nations leading the mobilisation of at least $300 billion annually. The Tropical Forest Forever Facility was officially launched at COP30 in Belem, Brazil, to make standing forests more valuable than cleared land.
facts: The NCQG on climate finance was formally established at COP29 in Baku.
Target: scale up climate funding to developing nations to at least $1.3 trillion per year by 2035.
Developed nations agreed to lead mobilisation of at least $300 billion annually by 2035.
The Baku-Belem Roadmap to 1.3T designed an institutional mechanism spanning the Azerbaijan and Brazil Presidencies.
The Tropical Forest Forever Facility (TFFF) was officially launched at COP30 in Belem, Brazil.
COP30 in Belem is widely termed the 'Amazon Forest COP'.
TFFF makes standing, living tropical forests more economically valuable than cleared land.
TFFF directly addresses the financial drivers of deforestation.

subtopics.title: India's Climate Targets and the Solar Alliance
subtopics.summary: India's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) set targets on emissions intensity, non-fossil power capacity and carbon sinks, and the updated NDC submitted in 2022 raised the 2030 goals. The status column shows that the 2030 non-fossil target had reached 52.57% by February 2026. The International Solar Alliance, launched by India and France in 2015, was officially established in December 2017.
facts: First NDC (submitted 2015): cut emissions intensity of GDP by 33-35% from 2005 levels by 2030.
Updated NDC (submitted 2022): cut emissions intensity of GDP by 45% by 2030.
Non-fossil fuel based installed electric power capacity: 40% by 2030 (first NDC), 50% (updated NDC).
First NDC: additional carbon sink of 2.5-3 billion tonnes CO2 equivalent by 2030 through forest and tree cover.
Status: 36% reduction in emissions intensity achieved by 2020.
Status: 52.57% non-fossil fuel based installed capacity achieved by February 2026.
Status: 2.29 billion tonnes CO2 equivalent additional carbon sink achieved by 2021.
International Solar Alliance (ISA) jointly launched by India and France in 2015 on the sidelines of COP-21 in Paris.
ISA was officially established on 6 December 2017, on the entry into force of the Framework Agreement.
ISA covers solar resource-rich states lying fully or partially between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn.

subtopics.title: Forest, Wetland and Restoration Drives in India
subtopics.summary: India runs several land-based programmes to expand and protect green cover. The National Mission for Green India aims to add forest and tree cover on 5 million hectares and improve quality on another 5 million hectares. The Aravalli Green Wall is a planned 1,400 km by 5 km green belt from Porbandar (Gujarat) to Panipat (Haryana), intended to halt desertification from the Thar Desert.
facts: National Mission for Green India (2014) is one of 8 missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change.
Green India Mission: increase forest/tree cover on 5 million hectares and improve quality on another 5 million hectares.
CAMPA funds promote afforestation and regeneration on waste, vacant and barren lands.
India expanded its Ramsar Site count to 100 as of now.
India ranks 3rd globally in net forest area gain over the past 15 years.
Project Tiger was launched in 1973 and Project Elephant in 1992.
MISHTI (Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats and Tangible Incomes) was announced in Union Budget 2023-24.
Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam: plant trees in memory of one's mother, linking emotional appeal with afforestation.
Aravalli Green Wall: 1,400 km x 5 km green belt from Porbandar (Gujarat) to Panipat (Haryana), inspired by Africa's Great Green Wall.
Aravalli purposes: halt desertification from the Thar Desert, restore degraded lands, improve air quality, biodiversity and climate resilience.

subtopics.title: Plastic Pollution, Cleanliness and Mission LiFE
subtopics.summary: Governments are negotiating an internationally legally binding instrument to end plastic pollution, through an Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee (INC) that has met in several cities since 2022. India's own efforts include the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, launched in 2014, and Mission LiFE, first introduced in 2021. Industry and project-level initiatives such as the India Plastics Pact and Project REPLAN add to these efforts.
facts: Negotiators are developing an internationally legally binding instrument to end plastic pollution worldwide.
INC sessions: Punta del Este, Uruguay (2022); Paris, France (2023); Nairobi, Kenya (2023); Ottawa, Canada (May 2024).
Swachh Bharat Abhiyan was launched by the PM on Gandhi Jayanti, 2 October 2014, in New Delhi.
Swachh Bharat aimed for a 'Clean India' by 2 October 2019, the 150th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi.
Bangladesh was the first country to ban thin plastic bags.
India Plastics Pact was launched in collaboration with the Confederation of Indian Industries (CII) and WWF.
Project REPLAN (REducing PLAstic in Nature) was launched by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC).
REPLAN process: waste plastic is collected, cleaned, chopped, beaten and treated for softness.
Mission LiFE is an India-led global mass movement for protecting and preserving the environment.
Mission LiFE was first introduced in 2021 by PM Modi at COP26 in Glasgow, and aims to mobilise at least 1 billion people for 2022-2027.

quizzes.passage: The booklet describes several environmental programmes in India, and this passage draws on a few of them. The Swachh Bharat Abhiyan was launched by the Prime Minister on Gandhi Jayanti in New Delhi, with the aim of making a Clean India by a date that marked the 150th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi. Over the years, the mission has evolved into a National Movement. India's Plastics Pact is the first of its kind in Asia and was launched in collaboration with the Confederation of Indian Industries and the World Wide Fund for Nature. It is a business-led initiative that seeks to transform the plastics packaging value chain for all formats and products. The Aravalli Green Wall Project draws its inspiration from Africa's Great Green Wall and proposes a green belt of 1,400 km by 5 km along the Aravalli Range. Its purposes include halting desertification from the Thar Desert and improving air quality and biodiversity. Its other stated purposes are restoring degraded lands and ecosystems and building climate resilience. Mission LiFE is another initiative that was first introduced by the Prime Minister at COP 26 in Glasgow. It is described as an India-led global mass movement that aims to nudge individual and collective action to protect and preserve the environment.
